title: Diagonal coefficient categories and integration diagrams
statement: For any scheme $Y$, put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $W=P\times_Y P$ and use the existing module-object category for a pulled-back commutative condensed coefficient $\Lambda$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Its unit is the regular coefficient module in degree zero, and its supported source is $S_\Lambda=\Delta_*\Lambda_P$. For specified modules $L_X$ on schemes, a diagonal diagram consists of universally normalized right-derived models, in the sense of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace], of $q_*,p_{1*},p_{2*}$, whose functors equal the canonical right-derived functors and whose full units on complexes coincide with the canonical right-derived units through these equalities; an arrow $S_\Lambda[0]\to L_W[2]$; traces $Rq_*L_P[2]\to\Lambda_Y[0]$ and $Rp_{i*}L_W[2]\to\Lambda_P[0]$; and the two integration equalities. The source of each integration map is identified by the actual ordinary composition map $p_i\Delta=1$ on underlying sheaves, followed by the universal right-derived unit, asserted invertible on this source. This defines data, not the assertion that such a diagram always exists.
